name: Zirl
kurzbeschreibung: Historic market town at the exit of the Inntal, featuring the Martinswand – a legendary via ferrata and a mystical rock face.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The market town of Zirl lies at 622 metres above sea level in the Tyrolean Upper Inn Valley within the district of Innsbruck-Land, about ten kilometres west of Innsbruck on the northern bank of the Inn River. Nestled against the dramatic limestone ramparts of the Karwendel Alps, the town is dwarfed by the sheer vertical rock faces of the Martinswand and the 2,541-metre Großer Solstein. Home to approximately 8,250 residents, Zirl forms a bustling municipal centre situated at a historic crossroads between the Inn Valley and the Scharnitz Pass. A mild, foehn-favoured valley climate has nurtured rich cultural heritage, world-class climbing terrain, medieval fortresses, and North Tyrol's most established viticulture.

Geschichte

Inhabited since the Hallstatt and Roman periods, the strategic Martinsbühel hill housed the Roman fortress of Teriolis along the Via Raetia. This name evolved into Zirl, first documented on 28 October 799 as Cyreolu. In 1499, Emperor Maximilian I famously became stranded on the sheer cliffs of the Martinswand while chamois hunting; according to legend, an angel in the guise of a shepherd guided him to safety, prompting the emperor to establish the Emperor Maximilian Grotto with a memorial crucifix. Overlooking the town stands the ruins of Fragenstein Castle, erected before 1209 by the Counts of Andechs and blown up during the War of the Spanish Succession in 1703. A religious gem is the neo-Romanesque Church of the Holy Cross, completed in 1848, renowned for its vivid Nazarene ceiling frescoes painted by local artist Franz Plattner. Historic hillside vineyards beneath Fragenstein have yielded Tyrolean wine since the 14th century.

Anreise

Zirl benefits from an exceptional transport location in central Tyrol. Motorists reach the town via the Inntal motorway A12 using exits Zirl Ost and Zirl West, alongside the federal highway B171. Approaching from Munich or Garmisch-Partenkirchen, the federal highway B177 crosses the Seefeld plateau and negotiates the notorious Zirler Berg with gradients of up to 16 percent down into Zirl. Train passengers use Zirl railway station on the Arlberg line, served every half hour by the Tyrolean S-Bahn from Innsbruck. In addition, Hochzirl station sits along the scenic Karwendelbahn mountain line, while frequent regional VVT buses connect to Innsbruck and Telfs.

Tipps

The towering Martinswand is a globally renowned rock climbing arena: the challenging Kaiser-Max-Klettersteig via ferrata tackles the cliffs in two demanding stages up to difficulty grade E. Leisure walkers can ascend along a secure path to the historic Emperor Maximilian Grotto, enjoying sweeping vistas across the Inn Valley. The ruins of Fragenstein Castle with their preserved keep make for a scenic walk. Nature lovers should not miss the rugged Ehnbachklamm gorge, featuring cascading waterfalls, historical weirs, and climbing crags. Inside the town, the Church of the Holy Cross dazzles with magnificent Nazarene frescoes by Franz Plattner, ideally followed by sampling local Zirl wines.
